Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1229 AM CDT Mon Aug 03 2026

Valid 041200Z - 051200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS IN SOUTHEAST
ARIZONA...SOUTH-CENTRAL COLORADO...NORTH-CENTRAL AND NORTHEAST NEW
MEXICO...AND PORTIONS OF THE CAROLINAS...

...SUMMARY...
Isolated severe storms capable of severe wind gusts and marginally
severe hail appear possible in southeast Arizona, south-central
Colorado, and north-central and northeast New Mexico Tuesday
afternoon and evening. Locally damaging winds may occur with
stronger storms in the Carolinas.

...Synopsis...

A broad, cyclonic flow regime is forecast from the northern Rockies
into the Great Lakes, to the north of an elongating upper high over
the Lower CO Valley into the southern Rockies. Within that pattern,
there is a model signal that a low-amplitude disturbance and
associated mid-level wind maximum will move through the northern
Plains and mid MO Valley. Elsewhere, an upper low centered over the
southern Appalachians Tuesday morning is expected to weaken while
slowly shifting north-northwest. 

At the surface, a front will move into the upper Great Lakes with
the boundary trailing southwest through the mid MO Valley into the
southern High Plains. A weak surface low may evolve along the front
over the mid or lower MO Valley Tuesday afternoon into evening. 


...Southeast Arizona...

Widely scattered thunderstorms are anticipated by mid afternoon
along the Gila Mountains and high terrain nearer to the
international border within a moderately unstable environment with
MLCAPE up to 1000-1500 J/kg. The presence of a deep, well-mixed
boundary layer will enhance evaporative cooling potential in the
sub-cloud layer with an associated risk for locally severe wind
gusts as storms advance southwest into the lower desert during the
late afternoon into evening. Some threat for marginally severe hail
may exist with the storms developing along the international border
owing to slightly stronger deep-layer shear.


...South-central Colorado and north-central and northeast New
Mexico...

A relatively small spatial corridor of modest instability and 30-35
kt of deep-layer shear is forecast to materialize in the lee of the
Sangre De Cristo Mountains Tuesday afternoon and evening. The
favored corridor extends from where the surface front intersects the
high terrain northward within the immediate post-frontal upslope.
Several of the 00Z CAMs indicate the potential for isolated to
widely scattered storms capable of a few occurrences of marginally
severe hail and/or locally severe wind gusts.


...Carolinas...

Forcing for ascent associated with the deep-layer low is expected to
contribute to an increase in thunderstorms through the day. Where
stronger heating can occur, the presence of a moist boundary layer
will support MLCAPE up to 1000-2000 J/kg. While stronger upper-level
winds are forecast within the eastern periphery of the low, vertical
shear through the lower half of the storm depth is expected to
remain relatively weak, limiting the potential for storm
organization. Nonetheless, steepening low-level lapse rates and a
high precipitable water may enhance wet microburst potential, with a
few damaging wind gusts possible.


...Middle and Lower Missouri Valley into the upper Midwest...

Consensus of the 00Z models suggests the majority of thunderstorm
activity will likely remain elevated to the north of the front in NE
and IA within a strongly sheared, but only marginally unstable
environment. Poor mid-level lapse rates are expected to limit any
severe hail threat. There is some model signal for isolated storm
development during the afternoon into evening along the front from
the lower MO Valley into southern/eastern WI. However, given that
there is considerable model variability in the degree of instability
ahead of the boundary, and that vertical shear will be somewhat
marginal across the warm sector, no probabilities will be included
in this forecast.

..Mead.. 08/03/2026

$$

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0224 PM CDT Sun Aug 02 2026

Valid 041200Z - 051200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PORTIONS
OF SOUTHEASTERN ARIZONA...

...SUMMARY...
Widely scattered severe storms capable of severe wind gusts appear
possible in southeast Arizona Tuesday afternoon and evening.

...Synopsis...
Broad troughing will continue across southern Canada into the
central US D3/Tuesday, with enhanced mid-level flow moving across
the Northern Rockies and Upper Great Lakes regions. A shortwave
trough will traverse the Mid-Missouri Valley late in the period as a
cold front shifts south and east from the Great Lakes/Midwest and
across the Central/Southern Plains.

...Southeast Arizona...
Strengthening easterly mid-level flow and lowering heights will aid
in thunderstorm development across the high terrain in southeastern
Arizona. Strengthening flow aloft will provide increased deep layer
shear for organization across the region. A deeply mixed and
moderately unstable air mass across the lower desert will support
potential for one or more clusters moving off the high terrain which
will be capable of damaging wind through the afternoon.

...Mid-Missouri Valley...
Several rounds of widely scattered thunderstorm activity is expected
across the Mid-Missouri Valley Tuesday. Elevated thunderstorm
activity will likely be ongoing near the start of the period near
the surface front. A corridor of moderate instability may develop
south of the front by afternoon from northeast KS into southern IA;
however, the absence of appreciable forcing mechanisms leads to
considerable uncertainty in whether any surface-based storms will
develop during the daylight hours. Better chances for development
will arrive with a shortwave trough passage late in the period. Poor
lapse rates and marginal instability leads to low confidence in
severe potential overnight, but a few stronger storms may produce
gusty winds and small hail given strong deep layer shear profiles.

..Thornton.. 08/02/2026

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0328 AM CDT Sun Aug 02 2026

Valid 051200Z - 101200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Day 4/Wednesday...

Broad troughing will exist from Hudson Bay into the north-central
U.S. with a belt of enhanced, cyclonic flow from the northern
Rockies through northern and central Plains into the upper Great
Lakes. At the surface, a front will advance through the upper Great
Lakes with the western extension of the boundary settling more
slowly south through the central into southern High Plains. 
Thunderstorms may be ongoing at 12Z across portions of the mid MO
Valley with lingering clouds and convective outflow potentially
modulating the location of the effective surface front and the
degree of instability ahead of it. The models suggest an area from
eastern KS into MO as being the most probable location for at least
isolated severe storms during the afternoon and evening hours. The
extent of the threat will likely be dependent on mesoscale details
yet to be known. As such, no area will be delineated in this
forecast.

Other areas of isolated severe storm potential will be in the
central High Plains and southeast AZ.


...Days 5 and 6/ Thursday and Friday...

A slight eastward shift of the mean trough position is forecast on
Thursday with some model signal for an embedded short-wave trough to
move through the Great Lakes. At the surface, there is some
suggestion that a weak front or wind shift will move into the
northern Mid-Atlantic during the afternoon with the trailing
extension of that boundary stretching through the mid MS Valley into
the southern High Plains. Ahead of that boundary, widespread 70+ F
dewpoints are expected from New England into the Mid-Atlantic and
Carolinas, leading to moderate to potentially strong instability.
The greatest potential for a few severe storms appears to be across
the Mid-Atlantic Thursday afternoon where the moderate instability
will coincide with a belt of 30-40 kt mid-level flow.

Some severe weather threat may also develop in the Ozark Plateau and
AZ Thursday afternoon and evening.  
 
On Friday, the above-mentioned Great Lakes short-wave trough is
expected to shear northeast across southern ON with 30-40 kt of
mid-level flow prevailing over the Northeast. The surface pattern is
somewhat disorganized with some semblance of a trough from southern
New England through the Mid-Atlantic coastal region. Moderate to
strong instability may again develop ahead of that feature,
supporting the potential for some severe weather threat during the
afternoon and early evening hours. However, the strongest vertical
shear is forecast to remain to the north of the stronger
instability, leading to uncertainty in the magnitude of the severe
threat.


...Days 7 and 8/Saturday and Sunday...

The various 00Z ensemble mean solutions indicate a slight eastward
shift of an upper low near Hudson Bay with low-amplitude troughing
and strengthening mid-level flow moving into the Northeast.
Southerly low-level winds within the western periphery of a surface
high positioned off the Atlantic Coast will maintain a moist and
unstable air mass beneath the strengthening winds aloft. As such,
some severe weather threat is expected to persist from the
Mid-Atlantic into New England this period.

Elsewhere, there is some model signal for a surface front to move
into the Midwest, where some severe weather potential may exist.

..Mead.. 08/02/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1254 AM CDT Mon Aug 03 2026

Valid 031200Z - 041200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS LATE THIS
AFTERNOON AND EVENING ACROSS PARTS OF NORTHERN MINNESOTA INTO
ADJACENT PORTIONS OF THE EASTERN DAKOTAS...

...SUMMARY...
Strong to severe thunderstorm development appears possible today
across parts of northern Minnesota into adjacent portions of the
eastern Dakotas, as well as across the eastern Arizona international
border vicinity and parts of the northern Mid Atlantic through
western New England.

...Discussion...
A compact, but fairly deep, lower/mid-tropospheric cyclone over the
Canadian Prairies is forecast to migrate across northern Manitoba
into western Hudson Bay today through tonight.  One initial trailing
cold front is already advancing into the northern Great Plains, with
a more substantive cold front approaching the international border
and forecast to overtake it by mid afternoon, roughly across the
northwestern Minnesota through southeastern North Dakota, central
South Dakota, and western Nebraska vicinity.  

As a notable upstream mid-level short wave trough accelerates across
the northern U.S. Rockies, toward northwestern Ontario, it appears
that a secondary surface low emerging from Wyoming will weaken while
migrating northeast of the Black Hills through the adjacent middle
Missouri Valley early today.  Another surface low may form along the
front across northern Minnesota into northwestern Ontario this
evening, but it appears that the most rapid deepening will occur
north of Lake Superior overnight.

To the south and southwest of the mid-level wave, models indicate
that mid-level ridging will build across the Southwest during the
day, with highest heights becoming centered along an axis across
southwestern through central Arizona into north central New Mexico
by late afternoon.

Within the downstream westerlies, a notable mid-level trough is
forecast to pivot east and northeast of the lower Great Lakes
through New England.  As it does, a remnant perturbation digging
toward the southern Appalachians may evolve into a weak mid-level
low across the Southeast, cut off from the westerlies.

...Northern Great Plains into Upper Midwest...
The influence of possible early period convection and associated
cloud cover on destabilization and convective potential later today
across parts of the central and eastern Dakotas into Minnesota
remains a bit unclear.  However, by mid to late afternoon, guidance
generally indicates that a fairly sharp quasi-stationary
near-surface baroclinic zone will evolve across northwestern
Minnesota through southeastern North Dakota.  It appears that this
may become a focus for at least a narrow corridor of modest
boundary-layer destabilization, coincident with strengthening south
to southwesterly lower/mid-tropospheric wind fields (including
30-40+ kt around 850 mb and 50-70 kt around 500 mb).  This may
provide a window of opportunity for strong to severe storm
development, including a couple of supercells, by this evening,
before the front overtakes the instability axis with the passage of
the frontal wave.

...Southeastern Arizona/adjacent New Mexico...
Low-level moisture appears likely to remain relatively modest across
central and southern Arizona, with strong daytime heating and mixing
lowering surface dew points through the mid to lower 50s F by late
afternoon.  However, along the southern periphery of the stronger
mid-level ridging, it appears that this may support at least
moderate boundary layer CAPE near the international border vicinity,
beneath 25+ kt east-northeasterly mid-level steering flow. 

The higher terrain either side of the southern Arizona/New Mexico
state border will provide potential for a more substantive
clustering of convection, which may propagate across and south of
the international border by early this evening.  If preceding
thunderstorm development, initially developing in the unstable
environment near the international border, does not generate too
much stabilizing outflow, it is possible that this could become
supportive of a swath of strong to severe wind gusts, aided by
evaporative cooling in a deeply mixed sub-cloud layer with 40-50 F
temperature/dew point spreads.

...Northern Mid Atlantic through western New England...
Along and ahead of a weak cold front, trailing a deepening surface
low migrating northeastward toward the lower St. Lawrence Valley,
boundary-layer destabilization will probably be slowed, if not
inhibited, by weak mid-level lapse rates and early day cloud
cover/precipitation,  However, strengthening deep-layer wind fields
and shear will potentially become more supportive of organized
thunderstorm development with a risk for damaging wind gusts and
perhaps a tornado or two, if pre-frontal breaks in cloud cover can
allow for sufficient destabilization with daytime heating.

..Kerr/Supinie.. 08/03/2026
